blocks.content: Mizoram's formation directly follows from the events of Chapter 3 — its Union Territory status (1972) and eventual full statehood (1987) are two more milestones in the same continuous political narrative culminating in the Peace Accord's implementation.

Prior to 1972, the Mizo Hills existed as the 'Mizo Hills District' (later 'Mizo District') of Assam, administered under Sixth Schedule autonomous-district arrangements (Chapter 5), even as the MNF-led insurgency (Chapter 3) continued.

On 21 January 1972 — the same date on which Manipur, Meghalaya and Tripura also achieved changes in status (Manipur and Tripura attaining full statehood, per the companion Manipur GS volume; Meghalaya having already become an autonomous state and then achieving full statehood on this same date, per the companion Meghalaya GS volume) — Mizoram was separated from Assam and constituted as a Union Territory in its own right, under the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971, with C. Chhunga (Mizo Union party) becoming its first Chief Minister on 3 May 1972.
As detailed in Chapter 3, the Mizoram Peace Accord of 30 June 1986 provided for Mizoram's elevation from Union Territory to full statehood as part of the settlement ending the MNF insurgency.

Mizoram formally became India's 23rd state on 20 February 1987, under the State of Mizoram Act, 1986 — attaining full statehood roughly 15 years after its 1972 Union Territory status, and, notably, on the SAME DATE as neighbouring Arunachal Pradesh (also created as a UT in 1972 and elevated to full statehood on 20 February 1987 under a companion Act) — making 20 February 1987 a shared statehood date for both states.

cells: Mizoram separated from Assam; becomes a Union Territory (North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971)
C. Chhunga (Mizo Union) becomes Mizoram's first Chief Minister (of the UT)
Mizoram Peace Accord signed, providing for future statehood (Chapter 3)
Mizoram attains full statehood (India's 23rd state), under the State of Mizoram Act, 1986 — same date as Arunachal Pradesh's statehood

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh BOTH attained full statehood on the SAME DATE — 20 February 1987 — a frequently tested shared-date fact linking this book to the wider North-East India state-formation chronology.

items: Mizoram became a UT on 21 January 1972 (same date as Manipur, Meghalaya and Tripura's status changes); C. Chhunga became first CM (of the UT), 3 May 1972.
Mizoram attained full statehood (India's 23rd state) on 20 February 1987, under the State of Mizoram Act, 1986 — the direct result of the 1986 Peace Accord.
Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh both became full states on the SAME DATE: 20 February 1987.
